translationRepairs: Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Huainan observation commissioner.
Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.
Chinese 出為湖南觀察使 names Hunan (湖南), not Huainan (淮南, which belongs to Jifu in s0026); the literal’s Huainan is a place-name error, and the proposed Hunan matches both the Chinese and the idiomatic.
Ku, style name Zhouqing, died as prefect of Wu.
Ku, style name Zhouqing, died as prefect of Wuzhou.
Chinese 終婺州刺史 is prefect of Wuzhou (婺州); bare Wu drops the prefecture name and is inaccurate, so Wuzhou is the correct repair.
Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wu.
Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wuzhou.
The literal likewise truncates 婺州 to Wu; ending as prefect of Wuzhou restores the full place name without other changes.
Youxin, with Reminder Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were hated by Fengji's pack for their attacks, hence the label "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
Youxin, with Reminder Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were Fengji's attack dogs and were hated for it, hence the label "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

為逢吉搏吠所憎 means Youxin and company were detested as Fengji’s barking attack dogs (they were the attackers), not hated by Fengji’s pack; the proposed literal reverses that agency error and matches the idiomatic sense.
When Fengji lost office and went to Huainan east circuit, he took Youxin as campaign Sima.
When Fengji lost office and went to the Shannan East Circuit, he took Youxin as campaign Sima.
Chinese 領山南東道節度 is the Shannan East Circuit command; Huainan (淮南) is a different circuit, so replacing Huainan east circuit with Shannan East Circuit corrects the place name.
When Fengji fell from power and took the Huainan east circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.
When Fengji fell from power and took the Shannan East Circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.
The literal’s Huainan east circuit likewise misreads 山南東道; Shannan East Circuit command is the accurate place-name repair.
Implicated in Tian You's case, he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
Implicated in Tian Pi's case, he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
田伾 is Tian Pi (伾 Pī); You is a misreading of 伾, and the proposed idiomatic corrects only that personal name.
For involvement in Tian You's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
For involvement in Tian Pi's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
The literal also has Tian You for 田伾; Tian Pi matches the character and pinyin, and the rest of the sentence is unchanged.
Ning passed the Mingjing, served as Linhuai chief clerk, quit office, returned home to Xia, and became Yang Cheng's closest friend.
Ning passed the Mingjing, served as Linhuan chief clerk, quit office, returned home to Xia, and became Yang Cheng's closest friend.
臨渙 is Linhuan (渙 huàn), not Linhuai (淮); the idiomatic place-name error is corrected by Linhuan.
He passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed chief clerk of Linhuai, resigned, returned to Xia, and became sworn friend with Yang Cheng.
He passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed chief clerk of Linhuan, resigned, returned to Xia, and became sworn friend with Yang Cheng.
The literal likewise misreads 臨渙 as Linhuai; chief clerk of Linhuan restores the correct county name.
Sons Zhituo, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all took the jinshi; Hangong shone brightest.
Sons Zhitui, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all took the jinshi; Hangong shone brightest.
知退 is Zhitui (退 tuì); Zhituo misreads 退, and the proposed idiomatic restores the correct given name while leaving the other sons unchanged.
Under Wenzong, Wei Chuhou ruled and condemned Wang for scheming toward secret posts and imperial intimacy; the uproar sent him to Qiongzhou as army aide.
Under Wenzong, Wei Chuhou ruled and condemned Wang for scheming toward secret posts and imperial intimacy; the uproar sent him to Zhangzhou as army aide.
貶漳州司戶參軍 is demotion to Zhangzhou (漳州); Qiongzhou would be 瓊州, so Zhangzhou is the correct place-name repair.

When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou held government and issued an edict that Wang, by treacherous shallowness, sought secret office and imperial favor, stirring public clamor, be demoted to Qiongzhou army aide.

When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou held government and issued an edict that Wang, by treacherous shallowness, sought secret office and imperial favor, stirring public clamor, be demoted to Zhangzhou army aide.
The literal also has Qiongzhou for 漳州; Zhangzhou army aide matches the Chinese demotion place.
